This module's only new regulatory content is the POA&M (plan of action and milestones) passage
itself, drawn from the same saved excerpt the first four modules already used — no new source was
independently fetched. The two internal links below are the direct inputs this module builds on
and the parallel it draws against; both were followed and confirmed to load correctly from this
session. Further external reading and a video follow them.

- **[NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, "Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-37r2.pdf)**
  (PDF, final, December 2018) — the document behind this lesson's one new quote, Task A-6's plan
  of action and milestones discussion, via the same saved excerpt in `sources/nist/` used in all
  four earlier modules. Curl-checked directly from this session: returns HTTP 200.

- **[Authorize and Monitor](../authorize-and-monitor/index.qmd)** — the previous module, where the
  Director's authorization decision and its exact 30-day remediation commitment (the systems
  administrator completing the first quarterly access review and reporting results to the
  Director) were put on the record. This module's POA&M entry is built field by field from that
  decision — nothing here is a new finding.

- **[CAPA: root cause to effectiveness
  check](../../quality-system-essentials/capa-root-cause-to-effectiveness/index.qmd)** — the
  `quality-system-essentials` module this lesson places its POA&M entry next to. Read it for the
  actual CAPA mechanics (root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, the effectiveness
  check) this lesson references by name but deliberately doesn't redevelop.

- **[Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) Overview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DX9C0VlrwYE)**
  (Optic Cyber, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A cybersecurity
  consulting firm's overview of what a POA&M is and contains. Industry training content, not a
  NIST publication and not blood-specific. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC: Risk Management Framework](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/risk-management/about-rmf)**
  — NIST's own landing page for the RMF, with links to SP 800-37 and related publications. Read it
  to see where the Authorize and Monitor steps sit in the framework's current official
  presentation. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST CSRC Glossary: plan of action and milestones](https://csrc.nist.gov/glossary/term/plan_of_action_and_milestones)**
  — NIST's short official definitions of the term, collected from its publications. Read it for a
  one-line, authoritative restatement of what the Task A-6 passage describes. Verified loading
  via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Q9(R1) Quality Risk Management](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/q9r1-quality-risk-management)**
  — FDA's page for the ICH Q9(R1) guidance, the quality-side risk framework this course compares
  RMF against in module 1. Read it when you want the primary source behind the CAPA-side
  vocabulary, rather than this curriculum's summary of it. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Atlassian: Problem Management in ITIL](https://www.atlassian.com/itsm/problem-management)**
  — a vendor-published ITSM explainer on problem management, the discipline this lesson's bridge
  compares POA&Ms and CAPAs to. It is a commercial vendor's guide, not ITIL's own text. Verified
  loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about tracking weaknesses to closure.

- **[CMS Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) Handbook](https://security.cms.gov/learn/cms-plan-action-and-milestones-poam-handbook)** (CMS Information Security and Privacy Program) — a practical government handbook showing how one large agency writes, tracks and closes POA&M items. Good concrete examples to set beside a CAPA. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Automating the RMF: A Necessary Evolution](https://www.isaca.org/resources/isaca-journal/issues/2025/volume-4/automating-the-rmf-a-necessary-evolution)** (ISACA Journal, 2025) — covers tooling that generates and tracks POA&Ms alongside other authorization documents. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Security Risk Assessment Methods: Quantitative & Qualitative](https://destcert.com/resources/risk-assessment-methods/)** (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP trainer) — helps you rate the risk of an open weakness so priorities and due dates are defensible. CISSP Domain 1. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Business Continuity (BCM) MindMap | CISSP Domain 7](https://destcert.com/resources/business-continuity-management-bcm-mindmap-cissp-domain-7/)** (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP trainer) — a Domain 7 view of managing risk you cannot yet eliminate, a useful companion to the idea of temporary compensating measures. CISSP Domain 7 (Security Operations). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
